## How the time is measured

Nobody is timed. The time is read afterwards, between the commits, the Pull Requests and the Pull Request comments of each repository: a lab ends when its Pull Request is merged, and runs from the end of the one before.

A break longer than 45 minutes is not counted, so a learner who stops for the night adds nothing. Work done in the org leaves no trace on GitHub, which makes every figure a low estimate.

Labs 1.1 and 1.2 install the tools and create the orgs before the repository exists. They are not measured, and Level 1 is counted from Lab 1.3.

Labs that share one Pull Request are measured together.

The fastest is the fastest time somebody could have done the lab in. A figure under five minutes, or under a quarter of the median, is two labs checked in a row and is set aside. The slowest is not shown: it is somebody who was interrupted.

The time a lab page announces is this median, rounded down to five minutes, and the time of a level is rounded down to a quarter of an hour. A lab measured with others takes its share of their time, and a lab fewer than 3 learners went through keeps its estimate. The pages are rewritten from the figures every week.
